chapter: Depression years and New Orleans trumpeters
title: Johnny Cotrera and Sharkey Bonano
summary: Brownlee comments on Johnny Cotrera's strong playing and possible resemblance to Sharkey, and on Sharkey's circuit of Blue Room and Vegas work.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: And Johnny Cotrera, I doubt if you know him, he's a trumpet.
Oh. Yeah. He did. I knew Johnny. He was one of them. Handsome Johnny?

He's a fine looking boy too. Very fine. Very powerful and had a very strong lip. Very fine. I liked his playing fine. I liked his playing a whole lot. I think he was, I think he tried to play a whole lot like Sharky. Didn't he? Or did he? I don't remember. Am I mixed up?
That's been 16 years since I've heard him.
Well, now you have a verifying memory for everything else. You should have remembered that. I'm not trying to quiz you.
Yeah, well, you see, at that time I didn't hear Sharky. I heard Johnny Cotrera before I heard Sharky.
Except on some records, you know, and it'd be hard for me to compare him. From that standpoint. Sharky wasn't doing, you might see, I don't think. Playing spots.
Well, he used to work that circuit. He used to go out to, I think he worked around out to, to Vegas.
He worked the Blue Room quite a little bit, too, around New Orleans. Then he'd go upstate. Then he'd switch over to, towards Vegas, going west. And then...
